topics.title: Founding of the Indian National Congress (1885) and the Early Phase
topics.hook: Founded in December 1885 at Bombay by A.O. Hume, with W.C. Bonnerjee as its first President, launching organised national political activity.
topics.story:
The Indian National Congress held its first session at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay from 28 to 31 December 1885. Seventy-two delegates attended. Retired British civil servant Allan Octavian Hume played a key role in bringing educated Indians together, often linked to the 'safety valve' theory.

Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee served as the first President. Early leaders included Dadabhai Naoroji (who proposed the name Indian National Congress), Pherozeshah Mehta, Dinshaw Wacha, and Badruddin Tyabji (who became the first Muslim President in 1887 at Madras).

The early phase (1885-1905) was led by Moderates who used constitutional petitions, prayers, and resolutions. Dadabhai Naoroji authored 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' exposing the 'Drain of Wealth' theory.

topics.title: Partition of Bengal (1905) and the Swadeshi Movement
topics.hook: Viceroy Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, triggering the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement across India.
topics.story:
Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on 20 July 1905, taking effect on 16 October 1905. The official reason was administrative efficiency, but the political motive was dividing Hindu-Muslim unity.

The day of partition (16 Oct 1905) was observed as a day of mourning (Raksha Bandhan and fasts urged by Rabindranath Tagore). The Swadeshi Movement adopted boycott of foreign goods, promotion of indigenous industries, and national education. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 'Vande Mataram' became the anthem. Partition was annulled in 1911 by King George V at the Delhi Durbar, when the capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi.

topics.title: Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) and Chauri Chaura Incident
topics.hook: Launched by Mahatma Gandhi at Nagpur Congress session (1920) alongside Khilafat Movement; abruptly suspended after Chauri Chaura violence in Feb 1922.
topics.story: Approved at Nagpur session in Dec 1920. Called for boycott of titles, schools, courts, and foreign cloth. Merged with Khilafat Movement led by Ali Brothers (Shaukat & Mohammad Ali). On 4 Feb 1922, a mob set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP), killing 22 policemen. Gandhi called off the movement on 12 Feb 1922.

passages.title: The Emergence of the Congress
passages.passage: In late December 1885, seventy-two educated Indian delegates assembled at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay to establish the Indian National Congress. Organised with the assistance of Allan Octavian Hume, a retired civil servant, the Congress elected barrister Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee as its inaugural President. The early political phase was dominated by Moderate leaders who relied on constitutional petitions and public speeches. Leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji exposed the economic consequences of British administration, formulating the famous Drain of Wealth theory. Over time, the organisation transformed into the vanguard of India's anti-colonial struggle.

questions.q: Where was the first session of the Indian National Congress held?
questions.explain: The first session was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay in Dec 1885.

questions.q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explain: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee) was the first President.

questions.q: Who authored 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' articulating the Drain of Wealth?
questions.explain: Dadabhai Naoroji authored the work exposing British economic exploitation.

questions.q: Who was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explain: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the 1887 Madras session.

questions.q: Who was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explain: Annie Besant presided at the 1917 Calcutta session (Sarojini Naidu was first *Indian* woman in 1925).
